_: Bounds the compare table is held to. All three are absolute limits: 'median' caps the magnitude of the signed median, 'abs_median' caps the median absolute error, which is the one that can fail when errors of opposite sign cancel, and 'p90' caps the 90th percentile of that absolute error, which is the one that can fail when a minority of rows is far out and the median is not. A dimension can sit inside both medians while nearly half its rows are outside the references' own spread. 'rows' is how many of the grid's rows survived censoring into that median, so a later run can tell whether it is comparing against the same population. Re-record only in the same change as the behaviour that justifies it.
_damper_abs_median_grid: damper.abs_median was deleted 2026-10-22 and re-recorded. The 6.25 it held sat between two quanta of a reading taken on a 5 ms grid: at the recording 18 of the 35 rows read |delta| <= 5 ms and 17 read >= 10 ms, so the median was the 18th row exactly, and any one row crossing a quantum moves the median from 5 to 10. Taking the rosin jitter off the patch moved two rows by one quantum (n48 v80 -5 -> -10, n44 v104 -5 -> 0) and the median to 10 while the signed median stayed -5 and the p90 25; that is the grid, not the release.
_vibrato_reading: stretch.p90 (was 1.0), tnr.abs_median (was 10.525) deleted 2026-10-23 and re-recorded when the measurement moved on both sides at once: under a vibrato the tuning is the fundamental's mean pitch, demodulated under its own FM extent, rather than the strongest spectral line within 80 c; a partial's level is its power summed over that FM extent rather than its peak bin; and a vibrato whose rate wanders, or whose line shares the pitch track with fast FM, now widens the tone-to-noise mask and is read at the band's RMS depth over its rate span. The reference was re-measured and the model is read with the same ruler, so these bounds were recorded under a ruler that no longer exists. A still tone reads as it did.
